name: Major service outages
question: Do major software services stay up?
metric: Incidents at 12 software services, last 12 months
solvedIf: Major outages become rare and short
trendLabel: Rolling 12-month total of incidents at 12 software services, one point per month.
rule: More incidents when these services report more than in the previous 12 months.

analysis.title: Which services are counted
analysis.intro: GitHub, Claude, DigitalOcean, Render, Netlify, MongoDB Cloud, Sentry, Discord, Dropbox, Bitbucket, Linode, Zoom.
points: AWS is not counted, because its public feed only covers recent incidents. It currently shows 9, going back to Mar 1, 2026.
Google Cloud is not counted, because its public feed only covers recent incidents. It currently shows 8, going back to Feb 27, 2026.
Northflank is not counted, because its public feed only covers recent incidents. It currently shows 25, going back to Jun 12, 2025.
Twilio is not counted, because its roughly 3,500 yearly notices would swamp the total. Railway is not counted, because we found no machine-readable incident history.
A service that reports more honestly can look worse, so this shows reported incidents, not true reliability.

scoreReason: Per git push: Down 42% since December 2024, when the data starts.
caution: The data behind this score starts in December 2024, so it misses the first 25 months after ChatGPT launched.

Since December 2024: the count is up 41%, down 42% per git push (what the score uses) and down 6% per developer. If AI agents make pushes grow without making software more reliable, the per-push reading flatters this signal.
Without the git push adjustment, this signal would score 0% instead of 23%.
chartNote: The solid line is the count. The dashed line is what the score uses: the same count divided by git pushes, with the starting month of the score set to 100. Pushes have grown faster than failures, so the dashed line can fall while the count rises.
